source_title: Enhancement and contextual modulation of visuospatial processing by thalamocollicular projections from ventral lateral geniculate nucleus
node_relevance_reason: Directly characterises vLGN GABAergic (VGAT+) projection to superior colliculus, with retrograde tracing showing abundant SC-projecting vLGN neurons.
summary: Mouse vLGN sends GABAergic thalamocollicular projections that give surround suppression of SC visuospatial processing; AAVretro from SC labels abundant vLGN (not dLGN) neurons, with axons mainly in superficial SC.
quotes: In the mammalian visual system, the ventral lateral geniculate nucleus (vLGN) of the thalamus receives salient visual input from the retina and sends prominent GABAergic axons to the superior colliculus (SC).
revealed abundant SC-projecting neurons in vLGN, but not in its neighboring region dLGN

In particular, the superficial layers of SC (sSC, the visual SC) appeared to be a major targeting area of vLGN axons, while the axons in the intermediate and deep layers of SC (i.e., the motor SC) were sparser

source_title: Divergent outputs of the ventral lateral geniculate nucleus mediate visually evoked defensive behaviors
section: Divergent vLGN outputs exert opposite influences on defensive behaviors
node_relevance_reason: Quantifies NT identity of vLGN->SC neurons (~90% Vgat+, ~65% Gad2+) and shows vLGN GABA->SC function in defensive behavior.
summary: Retrograde labeling from SC shows most vLGN SC-projecting cells are Vgat+ (~90%) and ~65% Gad2+, with ~10% Vglut2+; vLGN->SC is a separate population from vLGN->Re, and activating vLGN GABA->SC neurons reduces freezing.
quotes: The majority of vLGN cells that project to the SC were Vgat+ (~90%; i.e., GABAergic), which consists of both Gad2 and Gad1 cell types
We found that approximately two-thirds (~65%) of vLGN cells that project to the SC were Gad2+ cells.
Two-color retrograde labeling of vLGN cells that project to the SC (in green) or to the Re (in red) confirmed that the vLGN→SC and vLGN→Re circuits represent distinct vLGN output pathways

source_title: An autoradiographic study of the projections from the lateral geniculate body of the rat.
node_relevance_reason: Autoradiographic tracing shows a vLGN projection to ipsilateral SC (stratum opticum, griseum superficiale) but does not address NT type.
summary: Classic rat tracing: one of five major vLGN projections runs through the brachium of the SC to terminate in ipsilateral SC, most strongly in stratum opticum.
quotes: One dorsomedial projection coursed caudally from the vLGN through the brachium of the superior colliculus to terminate in the ipsilateral superior colliculus
The most strongly labeled portion of the superior colliculus was the stratum opticum.

source_title: A High‐Resolution Transcriptomic Atlas of Cell Types in the Ventral Visual Thalamus
node_relevance_reason: snRNA-seq of vLGN reports mostly GABAergic neurons including projection neurons and notes SC targets, without defining SC-projecting subtype.
summary: Most vLGN neurons are GABAergic including projection neurons; vLGN has >20 neuronal types but which are SC-projecting is unresolved.
quotes: most neurons in vLGN are GABAergic, including GABAergic projection neurons
Perhaps this is not surprising given the diversity of neuronal cell types that we identified here, although it remains unclear what percentage of these distinct cell types are projection neurons.

source_title: Diverse GABAergic neurons organize into subtype-specific sublaminae in the ventral lateral geniculate nucleus
section: | Do laminated retinorecipient circuits organize visual pathways through the vLGN?
node_relevance_reason: Defines vLGN GABAergic subtypes by markers but states projection targets of subtypes are unknown.
summary: Identifies transcriptionally distinct GABAergic vLGN subtypes in sublaminae, likely projection neurons, but lacks subtype-specific projection resolution (e.g. to SC).
quotes: Unfortunately, we do not yet have subtype specific resolution of vLGN projection neurons but hope that the data presented here will help to create a molecular toolkit for such circuit tracing in future studies.
Might the different transcriptionally distinct GABAergic cell types in vLGN each project to different downstream nuclei and contribute to unique functions and behaviours?

source_title: GABAergic cell types in the superficial layers of the mouse superior colliculus
section: | Projections from the SC to the LGN and PT
node_relevance_reason: Concerns GABAergic SC projections to vLGN (reverse direction), not vLGN->SC neurons.
summary: GABAergic SC cells project to vLGN, PT and PBG but not dLGN; relevant only as the reciprocal SC-vLGN connection.
quotes: account for the current findings that GABAergic projections from the SC innervate the vLGN, PT, and PBG but not the dLGN

source_title: Nuclei-specific differences in nerve terminal distribution, morphology, and development in mouse visual thalamus
node_relevance_reason: Region-level statement that vLGN projections avoid cortex and target midbrain without SC or GABAergic specificity.
summary: vLGN projections do not enter cortex and instead innervate hypothalamus, thalamus and midbrain structures.
quotes: projections from vLGN do not enter cortex and instead innervate an array of ipsi-and contralateral structures within hypothalamus, thalamus and midbrain [22]
